content.text:
{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_074bc1f357314d8da96c1ef84cf92b85",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-facing-data-retention-and-deletion-overview.json",
    "title": "Customer-Facing Overview: Data Retention, Deletion, and Residency (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Customer-Facing Overview: Data Retention, Deletion, and Residency (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)\",\n  \"space\": \"security-and-compliance\",\n  \"author\": \"Olga Petrov\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"security\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-09-18\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-14\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Daniel Carter\",\n    \"Marcus Lin\",\n    \"Naomi Feldman\",\n    \"Markus Klein\",\n    \"Lukas Meyer\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"customer-facing\",\n    \"data-retention\",\n    \"data-deletion\",\n    \"data-residency\",\n    \"hosted\",\n    \"dedicated\",\n    \"private\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook\",\n    \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-customer-overview\",\n    \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sso-saml-scim-and-rbac-capabilities\",\n    \"/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/redwood-enterprise-security-faq-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis page provides customer-facing language describing how Redwood Inference (\\u201cRedwood\\u201d) handles data retention, deletion, and data residency across our deployment modes:\\n- **Redwood API (Hosted)**\\n- **Redwood Dedicated (Dedicated capacity hosted by Redwood)**\\n- **Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem deployments)**\\n\\nIt is intended to be shared with customers in security reviews and RFP responses. If a customer requests evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report), follow the evidence request process referenced below.\\n\\n**Last reviewed:** 2026-02-14\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Definitions (what we mean by \\u201cdata\\u201d)\\nRedwood services may process and/or store the following categories of data:\\n\\n1) **Customer Content**\\n- Prompts, chat messages, uploaded context, and model inputs\\n- Model outputs (generated text)\\n- Embedding input text and embedding vectors\\n\\n2) **Customer Configuration Data**\\n- Account and workspace configuration\\n- API keys, project settings, rate limits\\n- Model routing and rollout policies (where applicable)\\n- SSO/SCIM configuration and RBAC assignments\\n\\n3) **Operational Metadata (typically non-content)**\\n- Request timestamps, request IDs, model name/version, token counts, latency metrics\\n- Status/error codes and infrastructure telemetry\\n\\n4) **Logs**\\n- **Platform logs** (service/application logs; generally exclude Customer Content by default)\\n- **Audit logs** (security-relevant events such as logins, key creation, RBAC changes)\\n\\n5) **Support / Customer Success Data**\\n- Tickets, emails, and attachments submitted to Support\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Summary: retention and residency by deployment mode\\nBelow is a high-level comparison; details follow in later sections.\\n\\n### Hosted (Redwood API)\\n- **Customer Content retention:** By default, Redwood does **not** persist Customer Content (prompts/outputs) as part of the product workflow. Content is processed to generate results and is not stored for model training.\\n- **Operational metadata retention:** Retained for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning.\\n- **Audit logs:** Available in the Console and/or export integrations depending on plan.\\n- **Residency:** Customers select a serving region (where available). We aim to keep in-scope data processing within the selected region, subject to the \\u201cResidency scope and limitations\\u201d section.\\n\\n### Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated)\\n- **Customer Content retention:** Same default posture as Hosted; Dedicated provides **tenant isolation** and **predictable capacity**.\\n- **Operational metadata and logs:** Similar categories; isolation boundaries are stronger than multi-tenant Hosted.\\n- **Residency:** Region selection and residency constraints are commonly supported as part of Dedicated deployments.\\n\\n### Private (Redwood Private: VPC / on-prem)\\n- **Customer Content retention:** Customer controls data-plane storage and retention. Redwood can support configurations that minimize or eliminate content persistence.\\n- **Operational metadata and logs:** Determined by deployment configuration; in many Private deployments, customers choose export destinations and retention.\\n- **Residency:** Primary mechanism for strict residency requirements. For on-prem / air-gapped use cases, all data-plane processing stays within customer-controlled infrastructure.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Customer Content: what we store (and what we don\\u2019t)\\n### Default posture\\nAcross Hosted and Dedicated, Redwood\\u2019s default configuration is designed to minimize persistence of Customer Content:\\n- **Prompts/inputs and model outputs are processed in memory to fulfill the request** and are not stored as durable application data by default.\\n- Redwood **does not use Customer Content to train** foundation models provided through Redwood services.\\n\\n### Important nuance (what customers often ask)\\n- **\\u201cDo you log prompts/outputs?\\u201d**\\n  - By default, Redwood\\u2019s standard operational logs are designed to avoid recording Customer Content.\\n  - Some debugging workflows may capture limited request context (e.g., truncated payloads) only when explicitly enabled under controlled access and time-bounded procedures, or when provided by the customer in a support ticket.\\n\\n- **Caching and performance features**\\n  - Redwood may use **in-memory caching** (e.g., KV/prefix caching) to improve latency and cost efficiency. These caches are **ephemeral** and are not intended as durable storage of Customer Content.\\n\\n- **Abuse prevention and fraud monitoring**\\n  - Redwood retains certain operational metadata (e.g., request identifiers, usage metrics) to protect service integrity. This metadata is distinct from storing full Customer Content.\\n\\nIf a customer requires strict \\u201cno content logging\\u201d commitments, confirm the specific deployment mode and plan, and validate the final language with Security/GRC.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Retention: operational metadata, logs, and audit logs\\nRetention can vary by deployment mode, plan, and configuration. When responding to a customer questionnaire, avoid stating a single number as universal unless confirmed for that customer\\u2019s plan.\\n\\n### Typical retention categories (Hosted/Dedicated)\\n**A) Operational metadata (non-content)**\\nRetained to operate the service, including:\\n- Request IDs, timestamps, model identifiers\\n- Token usage and billing-relevant metrics\\n- Latency and error rate telemetry\\n\\n**B) Platform logs (non-audit)**\\nRetained for troubleshooting and security monitoring. These logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.\\n\\n**C) Audit logs**\\nAudit logs record security and administrative events such as:\\n- User authentication events (SSO logins)\\n- API key creation/revocation\\n- RBAC changes\\n- Project/workspace configuration changes\\n\\n### Retention controls and options\\n- **Audit log retention** and **export options** may be configurable by plan (e.g., longer retention windows and export destinations available for Enterprise tiers).\\n- Export options may include customer-managed storage or SIEM integrations depending on deployment mode and configuration.\\n\\nFor details on event taxonomy and export patterns, see: **Audit Logging \\u2013 Customer Overview** (related page).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Deletion: how customers can request deletion and what it covers\\n### What \\u201cdeletion\\u201d means in practice\\nA deletion request generally applies to one or more of the following:\\n- **Customer Content** provided to Redwood services (if any is persisted through explicit configuration or support workflows)\\n- **Customer Configuration Data** (workspace/project settings, keys, and user access configuration)\\n- **Logs and operational metadata** (subject to retention policies and security requirements)\\n\\nDeletion requests should clearly specify scope:\\n- Entire organization/workspace deletion\\n- Specific project deletion\\n- Specific time window / dataset (rare; usually log-related)\\n\\n### Deletion workflow (Hosted/Dedicated)\\n1) Customer submits a request through their Redwood account team or Support.\\n2) Redwood confirms requester authorization and the scope of deletion.\\n3) Redwood executes deletion of applicable durable data stores and confirms completion.\\n4) Residual data may persist temporarily in:\\n   - Backups and disaster recovery systems until rotated\\n   - Logs retained for security, reliability, and legal/compliance obligations\\n\\n**Time to complete:** Redwood targets timely handling of deletion requests; actual timing depends on scope and any contractual obligations. If the customer has a contractual SLA for deletion, follow the contract.\\n\\n### Deletion workflow (Private)\\n- In **Private deployments**, customers typically control the data-plane and can delete data directly in their environment.\\n- Redwood can provide guidance on where data may exist (e.g., log locations, export destinations) based on deployment configuration.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Data residency: how region selection works\\n### What we mean by \\u201cdata residency\\u201d\\nCustomers commonly use \\u201cdata residency\\u201d to mean one or more of:\\n- **Where data is processed** (inference compute region)\\n- **Where data is stored** (logs, exports, customer configuration)\\n- **Where support personnel access data from** (administrative access location)\\n\\nRedwood addresses these separately to avoid ambiguity.\\n\\n### Hosted and Dedicated residency (region selection)\\n- Where available, customers can select a **serving region** for Hosted and Dedicated deployments.\\n- Redwood aims to keep **inference processing** within the selected region.\\n\\n### Residency scope and limitations (important)\\nEven when inference processing is region-scoped, some supporting systems may have different residency characteristics depending on plan and architecture:\\n- **Control plane data** (e.g., account administration, billing metadata, security administration) may be stored in a limited set of regions.\\n- **Global operational systems** (e.g., centralized monitoring/alerting) may receive non-content metadata.\\n- **Support workflows** may involve customer-provided content in tickets; customers can control what they share.\\n\\nIf a customer has strict regulatory requirements (e.g., EU-only, sector-specific rules), route the request to Solutions Engineering and Security/GRC for confirmation and deployment recommendation (often Dedicated or Private).\\n\\n### Private residency\\n- **Redwood Private (VPC)** is designed for customers who require stronger residency and network isolation controls.\\n- **On-prem / air-gapped** options can support the strongest residency posture because inference traffic and logs can remain entirely within customer-controlled infrastructure.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Customer controls (what customers can configure)\\nAvailable controls vary by deployment mode and plan, but commonly include:\\n\\n### Access and administrative controls\\n- SSO/SAML for Console access (where applicable)\\n- SCIM provisioning (where applicable)\\n- RBAC roles and permissions\\n- API key lifecycle controls\\n\\n### Logging and audit controls\\n- Audit log access and export options\\n- Retention windows (by plan)\\n- Destination control for exports (e.g., customer-managed storage/SIEM) in eligible plans/deployments\\n\\n### Data-plane controls (primarily Private)\\n- Network boundaries (VPC, private endpoints, on-prem)\\n- Customer-managed encryption keys (where applicable)\\n- Customer-controlled log pipelines and retention\\n\\nFor authoritative product capability specifics (and any limitations), see: **SSO/SAML/SCIM and RBAC Capabilities** and **Audit Logging \\u2013 Customer Overview**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Subprocessors, DPAs, and customer requests\\n- Redwood maintains a subprocessor list and provides contractual documentation (e.g., DPA) through standard procurement channels.\\n- If a customer requests a SOC 2 report or other audit evidence, do not email attachments ad hoc. Use the evidence request process:\\n  - **SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook** (related page)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## FAQ-ready wording (approved-style language)\\nUse or adapt the following in customer communications (ensure alignment with the customer\\u2019s deployment mode):\\n\\n**Q: Do you retain prompts and completions?**\\nA: \\u201cBy default, Redwood does not persist customer prompts or model outputs as durable application data. We process content to generate the response and retain operational metadata (e.g., timestamps, token usage, error codes) for service reliability, security, and billing purposes. Customers can choose deployment modes and configurations that provide stronger isolation and residency controls (Dedicated/Private).\\u201d\\n\\n**Q: Do you train models on our data?**\\nA: \\u201cNo. Redwood does not use customer content processed through the service to train foundation models.\\u201d\\n\\n**Q: Can you support EU data residency?**\\nA: \\u201cRedwood offers region selection for eligible services and can support EU-focused deployments depending on model and deployment mode. For strict residency requirements, Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private are typically recommended. We can review your requirements and confirm a compliant architecture.\\u201d\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Common pitfalls (what not to claim)\\n- Do not claim \\u201cwe never store any customer data\\u201d (we retain operational metadata, and customers may submit content via Support).\\n- Do not claim a universal retention duration across all plans and deployments.\\n- Do not claim \\u201call data always remains in-region\\u201d without scoping which data and confirming the target deployment.\\n- Do not promise roadmap items (e.g., new regions, new export destinations) in RFP responses.\\n\\nFor additional approved phrasing guardrails, reference the Security FAQ \\u201cwhat we do and don\\u2019t say\\u201d guidance (Sales Enablement).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Contact / escalation\\n- For customer-specific retention/residency confirmations: **Solutions Engineering** (route via deal channel) and **Security/GRC**.\\n- For evidence requests (SOC 2 report, pen test letters, security policies): follow the **SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook**.\\n\\nOwner: Security & Compliance (GRC)\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_074bc1f357314d8da96c1ef84cf92b85\"\n}",

{
  "title": "Customer-Facing Overview: Data Retention, Deletion, and Residency (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Olga Petrov",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-09-18",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-14",
  "reviewers": [
    "Daniel Carter",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Naomi Feldman",
    "Markus Klein",
    "Lukas Meyer"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "customer-facing",
    "data-retention",
    "data-deletion",
    "data-residency",
    "hosted",
    "dedicated",
    "private"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook",
    "/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-customer-overview",
    "/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sso-saml-scim-and-rbac-capabilities",
    "/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/redwood-enterprise-security-faq-2026"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This page provides customer-facing language describing how Redwood Inference (“Redwood”) handles data retention, deletion, and data residency across our deployment modes:
- **Redwood API (Hosted)**
- **Redwood Dedicated (Dedicated capacity hosted by Redwood)**
- **Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem deployments)**

It is intended to be shared with customers in security reviews and RFP responses. If a customer requests evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report), follow the evidence request process referenced below.

**Last reviewed:** 2026-02-14

---

## Definitions (what we mean by “data”)
Redwood services may process and/or store the following categories of data:

1) **Customer Content**
- Prompts, chat messages, uploaded context, and model inputs
- Model outputs (generated text)
- Embedding input text and embedding vectors

2) **Customer Configuration Data**
- Account and workspace configuration
- API keys, project settings, rate limits
- Model routing and rollout policies (where applicable)
- SSO/SCIM configuration and RBAC assignments

3) **Operational Metadata (typically non-content)**
- Request timestamps, request IDs, model name/version, token counts, latency metrics
- Status/error codes and infrastructure telemetry

4) **Logs**
- **Platform logs** (service/application logs; generally exclude Customer Content by default)
- **Audit logs** (security-relevant events such as logins, key creation, RBAC changes)

5) **Support / Customer Success Data**
- Tickets, emails, and attachments submitted to Support

---

## Summary: retention and residency by deployment mode
Below is a high-level comparison; details follow in later sections.

### Hosted (Redwood API)
- **Customer Content retention:** By default, Redwood does **not** persist Customer Content (prompts/outputs) as part of the product workflow. Content is processed to generate results and is not stored for model training.
- **Operational metadata retention:** Retained for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning.
- **Audit logs:** Available in the Console and/or export integrations depending on plan.
- **Residency:** Customers select a serving region (where available). We aim to keep in-scope data processing within the selected region, subject to the “Residency scope and limitations” section.

### Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated)
- **Customer Content retention:** Same default posture as Hosted; Dedicated provides **tenant isolation** and **predictable capacity**.
- **Operational metadata and logs:** Similar categories; isolation boundaries are stronger than multi-tenant Hosted.
- **Residency:** Region selection and residency constraints are commonly supported as part of Dedicated deployments.

### Private (Redwood Private: VPC / on-prem)
- **Customer Content retention:** Customer controls data-plane storage and retention. Redwood can support configurations that minimize or eliminate content persistence.
- **Operational metadata and logs:** Determined by deployment configuration; in many Private deployments, customers choose export destinations and retention.
- **Residency:** Primary mechanism for strict residency requirements. For on-prem / air-gapped use cases, all data-plane processing stays within customer-controlled infrastructure.

---

## Customer Content: what we store (and what we don’t)
### Default posture
Across Hosted and Dedicated, Redwood’s default configuration is designed to minimize persistence of Customer Content:
- **Prompts/inputs and model outputs are processed in memory to fulfill the request** and are not stored as durable application data by default.
- Redwood **does not use Customer Content to train** foundation models provided through Redwood services.

### Important nuance (what customers often ask)
- **“Do you log prompts/outputs?”**
  - By default, Redwood’s standard operational logs are designed to avoid recording Customer Content.
  - Some debugging workflows may capture limited request context (e.g., truncated payloads) only when explicitly enabled under controlled access and time-bounded procedures, or when provided by the customer in a support ticket.

- **Caching and performance features**
  - Redwood may use **in-memory caching** (e.g., KV/prefix caching) to improve latency and cost efficiency. These caches are **ephemeral** and are not intended as durable storage of Customer Content.

- **Abuse prevention and fraud monitoring**
  - Redwood retains certain operational metadata (e.g., request identifiers, usage metrics) to protect service integrity. This metadata is distinct from storing full Customer Content.

If a customer requires strict “no content logging” commitments, confirm the specific deployment mode and plan, and validate the final language with Security/GRC.

---

## Retention: operational metadata, logs, and audit logs
Retention can vary by deployment mode, plan, and configuration. When responding to a customer questionnaire, avoid stating a single number as universal unless confirmed for that customer’s plan.

### Typical retention categories (Hosted/Dedicated)
**A) Operational metadata (non-content)**
Retained to operate the service, including:
- Request IDs, timestamps, model identifiers
- Token usage and billing-relevant metrics
- Latency and error rate telemetry

**B) Platform logs (non-audit)**
Retained for troubleshooting and security monitoring. These logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.

**C) Audit logs**
Audit logs record security and administrative events such as:
- User authentication events (SSO logins)
- API key creation/revocation
- RBAC changes
- Project/workspace configuration changes

### Retention controls and options
- **Audit log retention** and **export options** may be configurable by plan (e.g., longer retention windows and export destinations available for Enterprise tiers).
- Export options may include customer-managed storage or SIEM integrations depending on deployment mode and configuration.

For details on event taxonomy and export patterns, see: **Audit Logging – Customer Overview** (related page).

---

## Deletion: how customers can request deletion and what it covers
### What “deletion” means in practice
A deletion request generally applies to one or more of the following:
- **Customer Content** provided to Redwood services (if any is persisted through explicit configuration or support workflows)
- **Customer Configuration Data** (workspace/project settings, keys, and user access configuration)
- **Logs and operational metadata** (subject to retention policies and security requirements)

Deletion requests should clearly specify scope:
- Entire organization/workspace deletion
- Specific project deletion
- Specific time window / dataset (rare; usually log-related)

### Deletion workflow (Hosted/Dedicated)
1) Customer submits a request through their Redwood account team or Support.
2) Redwood confirms requester authorization and the scope of deletion.
3) Redwood executes deletion of applicable durable data stores and confirms completion.
4) Residual data may persist temporarily in:
   - Backups and disaster recovery systems until rotated
   - Logs retained for security, reliability, and legal/compliance obligations

**Time to complete:** Redwood targets timely handling of deletion requests; actual timing depends on scope and any contractual obligations. If the customer has a contractual SLA for deletion, follow the contract.

### Deletion workflow (Private)
- In **Private deployments**, customers typically control the data-plane and can delete data directly in their environment.
- Redwood can provide guidance on where data may exist (e.g., log locations, export destinations) based on deployment configuration.

---

## Data residency: how region selection works
### What we mean by “data residency”
Customers commonly use “data residency” to mean one or more of:
- **Where data is processed** (inference compute region)
- **Where data is stored** (logs, exports, customer configuration)
- **Where support personnel access data from** (administrative access location)

Redwood addresses these separately to avoid ambiguity.

### Hosted and Dedicated residency (region selection)
- Where available, customers can select a **serving region** for Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
- Redwood aims to keep **inference processing** within the selected region.

### Residency scope and limitations (important)
Even when inference processing is region-scoped, some supporting systems may have different residency characteristics depending on plan and architecture:
- **Control plane data** (e.g., account administration, billing metadata, security administration) may be stored in a limited set of regions.
- **Global operational systems** (e.g., centralized monitoring/alerting) may receive non-content metadata.
- **Support workflows** may involve customer-provided content in tickets; customers can control what they share.

If a customer has strict regulatory requirements (e.g., EU-only, sector-specific rules), route the request to Solutions Engineering and Security/GRC for confirmation and deployment recommendation (often Dedicated or Private).

### Private residency
- **Redwood Private (VPC)** is designed for customers who require stronger residency and network isolation controls.
- **On-prem / air-gapped** options can support the strongest residency posture because inference traffic and logs can remain entirely within customer-controlled infrastructure.

---

## Customer controls (what customers can configure)
Available controls vary by deployment mode and plan, but commonly include:

### Access and administrative controls
- SSO/SAML for Console access (where applicable)
- SCIM provisioning (where applicable)
- RBAC roles and permissions
- API key lifecycle controls

### Logging and audit controls
- Audit log access and export options
- Retention windows (by plan)
- Destination control for exports (e.g., customer-managed storage/SIEM) in eligible plans/deployments

### Data-plane controls (primarily Private)
- Network boundaries (VPC, private endpoints, on-prem)
- Customer-managed encryption keys (where applicable)
- Customer-controlled log pipelines and retention

For authoritative product capability specifics (and any limitations), see: **SSO/SAML/SCIM and RBAC Capabilities** and **Audit Logging – Customer Overview**.

---

## Subprocessors, DPAs, and customer requests
- Redwood maintains a subprocessor list and provides contractual documentation (e.g., DPA) through standard procurement channels.
- If a customer requests a SOC 2 report or other audit evidence, do not email attachments ad hoc. Use the evidence request process:
  - **SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook** (related page)

---

## FAQ-ready wording (approved-style language)
Use or adapt the following in customer communications (ensure alignment with the customer’s deployment mode):

**Q: Do you retain prompts and completions?**
A: “By default, Redwood does not persist customer prompts or model outputs as durable application data. We process content to generate the response and retain operational metadata (e.g., timestamps, token usage, error codes) for service reliability, security, and billing purposes. Customers can choose deployment modes and configurations that provide stronger isolation and residency controls (Dedicated/Private).”

**Q: Do you train models on our data?**
A: “No. Redwood does not use customer content processed through the service to train foundation models.”

**Q: Can you support EU data residency?**
A: “Redwood offers region selection for eligible services and can support EU-focused deployments depending on model and deployment mode. For strict residency requirements, Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private are typically recommended. We can review your requirements and confirm a compliant architecture.”

---

## Common pitfalls (what not to claim)
- Do not claim “we never store any customer data” (we retain operational metadata, and customers may submit content via Support).
- Do not claim a universal retention duration across all plans and deployments.
- Do not claim “all data always remains in-region” without scoping which data and confirming the target deployment.
- Do not promise roadmap items (e.g., new regions, new export destinations) in RFP responses.

For additional approved phrasing guardrails, reference the Security FAQ “what we do and don’t say” guidance (Sales Enablement).

---

## Contact / escalation
- For customer-specific retention/residency confirmations: **Solutions Engineering** (route via deal channel) and **Security/GRC**.
- For evidence requests (SOC 2 report, pen test letters, security policies): follow the **SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook**.

arguments.title: Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule
arguments.content:
# Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule

**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  
**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  
**Revision:** 1 (baseline)  
**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park

## Rule

Use the following statements for Hosted API inquiries:

- By default, prompts, inputs, and model outputs are processed to fulfill the request and are not persisted as durable application data. Redwood does not use Customer Content processed through the service to train foundation models.
- Redwood retains non-content operational metadata for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning. Platform logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.
- In-memory caches are ephemeral and are not intended as durable Customer Content storage.
- A customer may request deletion through its account team or Support. Redwood verifies authorization and scope, deletes applicable durable stores, and confirms completion.
- Residual data can remain temporarily in backups/disaster-recovery systems until rotation and in logs required for security, reliability, legal, or compliance purposes.
- Where available, customers may select a serving region. Redwood aims to keep inference processing in that region, but control-plane data, centralized non-content monitoring, and Support workflows can have different residency characteristics.
- Retention and audit-log controls vary by plan and configuration.

## Do not promise

Do not state a universal retention period, deletion SLA, backup-purge deadline, certificate format, or that all data always remains in-region unless the customer's contract and deployment have been validated.

## Explicit unknowns

The current approved overview does not establish:

- a Hosted-wide time to delete active data;
- a maximum time to remove data from backups or disaster-recovery media;
- tenant-termination-specific sequencing;
- whether deletion confirmation includes backup exhaustion;
- a Hosted-wide cross-region replication rule;
- a universal audit-log retention period.

## Validation steps before answering a customer

1. Confirm the request scope: organization, workspace, project, dataset, time window, and data class.
2. Confirm requester authorization.
3. Check the customer's plan, deployment configuration, DPA/addenda, and deletion/residency SLA.
4. For strict residency or sector-specific requirements, route to Solutions Engineering and Security/GRC.
5. For SOC 2 or other controlled evidence, follow the approved evidence-request process.
6. Record only the contract-backed wording in the customer response.

## Evidence

- [E1] Customer-Facing Overview: Data Retention, Deletion, and Residency (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), published 2026-02-14 — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-facing-data-retention-and-deletion-overview.json` (document `dsid_074bc1f357314d8da96c1ef84cf92b85`).

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule\nSource: Platform & Console policy\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-v1\n\n# Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule\n\n**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  \n**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  \n**Revision:** 1 (baseline)  \n**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park\n\n## Rule\n\nUse the following statements for Hosted API inquiries:\n\n- By default, prompts, inputs, and model outputs are processed to fulfill the request and are not persisted as durable application data. Redwood does not use Customer Content processed through the service to train foundation models.\n- Redwood retains non-content operational metadata for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning. Platform logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.\n- In-memory caches are ephemeral and are not intended as durable Customer Content storage.\n- A customer may request deletion through its account team or Support. Redwood verifies authorization and scope, deletes applicable durable stores, and confirms completion.\n- Residual data can remain temporarily in backups/disaster-recovery systems until rotation and in logs required for security, reliability, legal, or compliance purposes.\n- Where available, customers may select a serving region. Redwood aims to keep inference processing in that region, but control-plane data, centralized non-content monitoring, and Support workflows can have different residency characteristics.\n- Retention and audit-log controls vary by plan and configuration.\n\n## Do not promise\n\nDo not state a universal retention period, deletion SLA, backup-purge deadline, certificate format, or that all data always remains in-region unless the customer's contract and deployment have been validated.\n\n## Explicit unknowns\n\nThe current approved overview does not establish:\n\n- a Hosted-wide time to delete active data;\n- a maximum time to remove data from backups or disaster-recovery media;\n- tenant-termination-specific sequencing;\n- whether deletion confirmation includes backup exhaustion;\n- a Hosted-wide cross-region replication rule;\n- a universal audit-log retention period.\n\n## Validation steps before answering a customer",

# Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule

**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  
**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  
**Revision:** 1 (baseline)  
**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park

## Rule

Use the following statements for Hosted API inquiries:

- By default, prompts, inputs, and model outputs are processed to fulfill the request and are not persisted as durable application data. Redwood does not use Customer Content processed through the service to train foundation models.
- Redwood retains non-content operational metadata for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning. Platform logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.
- In-memory caches are ephemeral and are not intended as durable Customer Content storage.
- A customer may request deletion through its account team or Support. Redwood verifies authorization and scope, deletes applicable durable stores, and confirms completion.
- Residual data can remain temporarily in backups/disaster-recovery systems until rotation and in logs required for security, reliability, legal, or compliance purposes.
- Where available, customers may select a serving region. Redwood aims to keep inference processing in that region, but control-plane data, centralized non-content monitoring, and Support workflows can have different residency characteristics.
- Retention and audit-log controls vary by plan and configuration.

## Do not promise

Do not state a universal retention period, deletion SLA, backup-purge deadline, certificate format, or that all data always remains in-region unless the customer's contract and deployment have been validated.

## Explicit unknowns

The current approved overview does not establish:

- a Hosted-wide time to delete active data;
- a maximum time to remove data from backups or disaster-recovery media;
- tenant-termination-specific sequencing;
- whether deletion confirmation includes backup exhaustion;
- a Hosted-wide cross-region replication rule;
- a universal audit-log retention period.

Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?\\n\\n1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?\\n2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?\\n3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?\\n4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?\\n5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?\\n\\nI attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.\\n\\nThanks,\\nEmma Lopez\\nSecurity & Compliance\\nCrestline Health\\n\\nAttachment: crestline-sq.pdf (application/pdf)\",\n    \"From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nCc: \\nDate: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nTeam \\u2014 forwarding Crestline's three-page SQ. They need short, precise answers for their board packet (deadline Tue COB). I drafted a proposal below but want confirmation on retention numbers and the phrasing around backups + purge timelines before I send.\\n\\nMain points to confirm:\\n- Default store region for hosted API (our standard tenancy mapping)\\n- Defaults for request logs vs embeddings vs model artifacts (we have flexibility for enterprise contracts)\\n- Wipe timeline for primary vs backups (we guarantee purge of primary within X days; full backup scrub may take longer)\\n- Language around KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys\\n\\nI attached an internal data-residency-matrix and a suggested doc (crestline_answers_v1.docx). Please reply with any edits.\\n\\nThanks,\\nOlga\\nHead of Solutions - CSM Escalations\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachments: crestline-sq.pdf, data-residency-matrix.xlsx, crestline_answers_v1.docx\\n\\nOn Sat, 30 May 2026 at 09:12, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health> wrote:\\n> Hi Olga,\\n> \\n> We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?\\n> \\n> [snip]\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nOlga \\u2014 draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.\\n\\n1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self\\u2011serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign\\u2011up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).\\n\\n2) Default retention windows (hosted API)\\n- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.\\n- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.\\n- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.\\n- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine\\u2011tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.\\n\\n3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines\\n- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.\\n- Backups / long\\u2011term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross\\u2011region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.\\n\\n4) Backups & cross\\u2011region replication\\n- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU\\u2011only custody we ensure backups remain in\\u2011region; cross\\u2011region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\\n- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.\\n\\n5) Key management & auditability\\n- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer\\u2011managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.\\n- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.\\n\\nNotes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30\\u2011day primary purge / 90\\u2011day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.\\n\\nIf that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.\\n\\n\\u2014 Karthik\\nDirector, Infrastructure Product\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachment: redwood-hosted-arch.pdf\\n\\nOn Sat, 30 May 2026 at 10:02, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:\\n> Team \\u2014 forwarding Crestline's three\\u2011page SQ.\\n> [snip]\",\n    \"From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>, security@crestline.health\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nHi Emma \\u2014 thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I\\u2019ve attached a one\\u2011page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.\\n\\nSummary answers (for packet)\\n\\u2022 Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy\\u2019s primary region. Self\\u2011serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU\\u2011only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.\\n\\u2022 Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.\\n\\u2022 Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.\\n\\u2022 Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU\\u2011only contracts cross\\u2011region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).\\n\\u2022 KMS & audit: Encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; enterprise customers may use customer\\u2011managed keys or HSMs. Deletion/erasure events are logged in the audit trail (365\\u2011day retention) and can be surfaced in the console or delivered as an export for enterprise customers.\\n\\nAttachments: crestline_answers_v1.docx (draft answers), data-residency-matrix.xlsx, redwood-hosted-arch.pdf\\n\\nNext steps: If that looks good I\\u2019ll send a formal addendum for EU tenancy pinning and CMK options. Otherwise send any edits and we\\u2019ll update the doc.\\n\\nBest,\\nOlga Petrov\\nHead of Solutions - CSM Escalations\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nOn Mon, 1 Jun 2026 at 11:24, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:\\n> Olga \\u2014 draft answers and rationale below.\\n> [snip]\"\n  ],\n  \"original_location\": \"gmail/olga_petrov/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3\"\n}",

    "From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Olga,

We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?

1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?
3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?
4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?
5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?

I attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.

Thanks,
Emma Lopez
Security & Compliance
Crestline Health

Attachment: crestline-sq.pdf (application/pdf)",
    "From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Team — forwarding Crestline's three-page SQ. They need short, precise answers for their board packet (deadline Tue COB). I drafted a proposal below but want confirmation on retention numbers and the phrasing around backups + purge timelines before I send.

Main points to confirm:
- Default store region for hosted API (our standard tenancy mapping)
- Defaults for request logs vs embeddings vs model artifacts (we have flexibility for enterprise contracts)
- Wipe timeline for primary vs backups (we guarantee purge of primary within X days; full backup scrub may take longer)
- Language around KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys

I attached an internal data-residency-matrix and a suggested doc (crestline_answers_v1.docx). Please reply with any edits.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Solutions - CSM Escalations
Redwood Inference

On Sat, 30 May 2026 at 09:12, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health> wrote:
> Hi Olga,
>

>

    "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Olga — draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.

1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self‑serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign‑up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.
- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine‑tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.

3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines
- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.
- Backups / long‑term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross‑region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.

4) Backups & cross‑region replication
- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU‑only custody we ensure backups remain in‑region; cross‑region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.

5) Key management & auditability
- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer‑managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.
- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.

Notes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30‑day primary purge / 90‑day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.

If that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

On Sat, 30 May 2026 at 10:02, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I’ve attached a one‑page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.

Summary answers (for packet)
• Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy’s primary region. Self‑serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU‑only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.
• Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.
• Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.
• Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU‑only contracts cross‑region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).
• KMS & audit: Encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; enterprise customers may use customer‑managed keys or HSMs. Deletion/erasure events are logged in the audit trail (365‑day retention) and can be surfaced in the console or delivered as an export for enterprise customers.

Attachments: crestline_answers_v1.docx (draft answers), data-residency-matrix.xlsx, redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

Next steps: If that looks good I’ll send a formal addendum for EU tenancy pinning and CMK options. Otherwise send any edits and we’ll update the doc.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions - CSM Escalations
Redwood Inference

document.title: Data residency & backup sweep: backup deletion propagation and confirmation
document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "thr-20260807-8f4b",
  "mailbox_owner": "rishi_malhotra",
  "subject": "Data residency & backup sweep: backup deletion propagation and confirmation",
  "participants_internal": [
    "rishi_malhotra",
    "monica_patel",
    "aditya_rao"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "security@acmehealth.com (Acme Health)",
    "procurement@acmehealth.com (Acme Health)"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2026-08-01T16:12:00Z",
  "last_email_at": "2026-08-03T18:04:00Z",
  "thread_type": "security_compliance",
  "related_account": "Acme Health",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "backup_policy_matrix.xlsx",
    "audit_log_export.csv"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.redwood.com/secure/ACME-backup-playbook-2026"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: security@acmehealth.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Backup retention & deletion propagation questions for PII/PHI workloads

Hi Rishi,

We're finalizing our vendor assessment for backup and deletion controls before procurement. A few implementation-level questions so we can put definitive language into the contract and MSA:

1) When an end-user record is deleted via the Redwood API (Customer request or on retention expiry), how long can copies of that data exist in backups or snapshots? Please list both: (a) hosted (Redwood-managed) snapshot retention windows, and (b) cross-region replication copies.

2) Does Redwood support targeted deletion from backups (for example: remove specific object keys or snapshots associated with a given customer) vs only rolling retention windows? If targeted deletion is supported, what is the expected maximum propagation time and proof artifacts we can receive?

3) For immutable/append-only snapshots (WORM-style), can you describe how deletion requests interact with immutability settings and whether snapshot immutability can be scoped per-customer?

4) For encrypted backups, is the encryption keys lifecycle under Redwood control or can keys be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key)? How does key deletion affect ability to recover older backups?

5) We need an auditable export that shows when a deletion request was received, when the dataset was purged from primary storage, and the timestamp when the backup sweep removed the data. Can you provide a sample CSV or export format and an estimated time-to-delivery for such an export after deletion?

We're on a compressed timeline for our security board next week. Please include technical owners in your reply if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Moran
Senior Security Manager
Acme Health
[sent from personal device]
",
    "From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: security@acmehealth.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 01:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion propagation questions for PII/PHI workloads

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Infra & DR) and Aditya (Customer Security lead) to ensure we cover operational and contractual pieces. High-level answers below; Monica will follow with the implementation timings and audit format.

1) Retention windows (hosted): standard snapshots are retained for 90 days by default; we offer configurable retention down to 0 days with a minimum 24-hour journal for operational safety. Cross-region replicas follow the source retention policy but may retain metadata for up to an additional 7 days for replication reconciliation. For customers requiring strict residency, we can pin backups to a region and prevent cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled.

2) Targeted deletion: We support targeted deletion from backup chains in two forms: (A) metadata-driven tombstone removal where we scrub object references tied to a customer and (B) snapshot rehydration + selective re-write where a new snapshot is created excluding the deleted objects and the old snapshot is scheduled for secure purge. Typical propagation windows: tombstone-based scrubs complete within 24–72 hours; snapshot rehydrate-and-purge flows can take 3–10 days depending on dataset size. We can provide signed attestations listing affected snapshot IDs and completion timestamps.

3) Immutable snapshots: Our default immutable snapshots are designed for compliance use-cases and are time-bound (WORM for N days). Immutability can be scoped per-customer when using Dedicated or Private deployments; for hosted customers immutability is available but with admin-level controls in our compliance team to enable per-account policies. Deletion requests against immutable snapshots require a separate governance flow and, where allowed, are handled via a controlled purge where we log approvals, the KMS operation, and the resulting object removal. That process adds latency (typically 7–30 days depending on legal/contractual approvals).

4) Keys: We offer both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations. If a customer deletes their KMS key, older backups encrypted with that key become unrecoverable unless a key-escrow/rotation policy was established. We recommend keeping a key-rotation/escrow plan in the contract for long retention windows.

5) Audit exports: Monica will attach a sample CSV schema. We can produce the export within 48 business hours after a confirmed purge completes. The export includes: request_id, customer_id, affected_snapshots, deletion_request_ts, primary_purge_ts, backup_sweep_completion_ts, operator_id, and S3/object-store object ids.

I'll let Monica add the nitty-gritty and sample artifacts. Happy to jump on a 30min call if that helps the board prep.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
",
    "From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: security@acmehealth.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion propagation questions for PII/PHI workloads

Hi Alex — technical follow-up with exact timings and the sample export attached. See the two attachments referenced below (backup_policy_matrix.xlsx and audit_log_export.csv). Key points: 

- Hosted default retention: 90d snapshots; journal (immutable operation log) retained 7d. Configurable to 0d min (24h safety journal).
- Cross-region replication: disabled by default for region-locked accounts. If enabled, replication metadata retention is +7d buffer.
- Targeted deletion mechanics:
  * Tombstone scrub: background job marks object refs; scrub job removes objects from incremental blocks. Completion: 24–72 hours for datasets ≤ 5TB, scales linearly.
  * Rehydrate & rewrite: for objects embedded in immutable snapshot chains we rehydrate to ephemeral nodes, rewrite snapshot excluding objects, then schedule secure purge of old snapshot blobs. Completion: 3–10 days typical (dataset dependent).
- Immutability and governance: For hosted customers with compliance needs we run an approval flow (security team sign-off + KMS operation audit). For Dedicated/Private customers immutability policies are customer-configurable.
- KMS/BYOK: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via KMIP. If customer-managed key is rotated but not deleted, we can still rewrap keys for restores; deletion of the key makes older backups unrecoverable.

Audit export fields (CSV headers provided in attached audit_log_export.csv): request_id, customer_id, deletion_initiator, deletion_type, primary_delete_ts, tombstone_scrub_start_ts, tombstone_scrub_end_ts, snapshot_rewrite_start_ts, snapshot_rewrite_end_ts, backup_sweep_completion_ts, operator, verification_hash, notes. Example row included for a test deletion (timestamps in UTC).

Proof artifacts we can deliver: signed attestations (P7S) for purge completion, CSV export, and S3 object manifests (if requested). We can also provide a short SLA clause for purge windows if you need contractual language.

Next steps for procurement: if you share the target retention/deletion constraints we will produce a short one-page compliance statement plus the CSV export sample you can drop into your vendor questionnaire. We can turn the statement around within 48 hours.

Attachments referenced:
- backup_policy_matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping retention/policy to deployment type and timelines)
- audit_log_export.csv (sample export row + field descriptions)

Regards,
Monica Patel
Staff Engineer, Infrastructure & DR | Redwood Inference
",
    "From: procurement@acmehealth.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 18:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion propagation questions for PII/PHI workloads

Rishi / Monica — thanks, this is exactly what we needed. Two quick asks from procurement side before we close the PO: 

1) Can you provide the one-page compliance statement (we'll attach it to our vendor packet)?
2) Please include the sample CSV (we received the one-row example in the email but would like the full template as a downloadable file).

We have a conditional clause: for our BAA we need assurance that targeted deletion (tombstone or rehydrate) completes within 30 days and that Redwood will provide a signed attestation within 5 business days of completion. Can you confirm acceptance or propose alternate language?

If accepted, we'll finalize the PO today.

Thanks — Laura Schmidt
Procurement Lead | Acme Health
",
    "On Mon, 03 Aug 2026 at 19:10 Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:

> Laura / Alex — we can commit to targeted deletion completing within 30 days for datasets under 50TB and to provide a signed attestation within 5 business days after purge completion. For larger datasets we'll include a scaled timeline in the one-page compliance statement. Monica will attach the formal statement and the full CSV template within 24 hours.
> 
> - Rishi
"

    "messages"
  ],

arguments.content:
# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency — support rule

**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  
**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  
**Revision:** 2 (corrected; replaces revision 1)  
**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park

## Canonical Hosted defaults

Use these defaults only when the customer's contract or configured policy does not replace them:

- Request/response payloads: retained 30 days by default.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: retained 14 days by default.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly persists them.
- Model artifacts, including fine-tuned artifacts: retained until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default cadence, while the maximum default backup-retention/full-scrub window is 90 days.
- Deletion and erasure audit events: retained 365 days by default and available through the Console or export for eligible enterprise accounts.
- Customer Content is not used to train Redwood foundation models.

Retention can be changed by plan, configuration, or contract. Do not imply that the default payload retention is zero.

## Verified erasure or tenant termination

1. Verify requester authorization and exact scope.
2. Stop serving the terminated tenant immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge.
3. Purge primary data within 30 days after the verified erasure request or tenant termination.
4. Scrub backups and replicated snapshots within 90 days. This window accounts for backup lifecycle and cross-region replication.
5. Provide a deletion attestation on request after completion.

Later infrastructure evidence describes targeted backup deletion through tombstone scrubs or snapshot rehydration/rewrite. Those paths can finish sooner, but their timing depends on dataset size, snapshot immutability, governance, and the customer's agreement. Do not convert typical 24–72-hour or 3–10-day mechanics into a universal SLA. Evidence should distinguish the primary-delete timestamp from the backup-sweep completion timestamp.

## Residency and cross-region behavior

- Hosted data is persisted in the tenant's primary region.
- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA and configuration.
- For an EU-only/region-locked contractual commitment, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Region selection alone does not prove that control-plane data, non-content global monitoring, or Support-submitted content has the same residency boundary.

## Evidence available for deletion

Deletion/erasure events are auditable. Depending on plan and contract, evidence can include a completion attestation, Console record, audit export, request ID, primary-purge timestamp, backup-sweep completion timestamp, operator ID, affected snapshot/object identifiers, and a verification hash. Do not promise a particular certificate format or delivery deadline unless it is contracted.

## Remaining unknowns and exceptions

The available evidence does not establish:

- that every customer has the same configured retention values;
- a universal sub-30-day primary-purge SLA or sub-90-day backup-purge SLA;
- that snapshot immutability can always be overridden;
- a universal evidence format or attestation-delivery time;
- that legal or compliance holds can never delay deletion;
- that all control-plane, telemetry, or Support data is tenant-region bound.

## Validation steps before customer use

1. Confirm organization/workspace/project, data classes, and whether the request is deletion, termination, retention expiry, or residency review.
2. Confirm authorization and any required export-before-delete instruction.
3. Inspect the customer's order form, DPA/BAA, residency addendum, retention configuration, DR configuration, and legal-hold status.
4. Confirm whether cross-region DR is enabled and enumerate every replica and snapshot class.
5. Track separate milestones for primary purge and backup-sweep completion.
6. Route exceptions and strict residency requirements to Solutions Engineering and Security/GRC.
7. Use the controlled evidence-request process for SOC 2 and related materials.

## Evidence

- [E1] Customer-Facing Overview: Data Retention, Deletion, and Residency, published 2026-02-14 — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-facing-data-retention-and-deletion-overview.json` (`dsid_074bc1f357314d8da96c1ef84cf92b85`).
- [E2] Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — approved customer security-questionnaire response, 2026-06-02 — `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json` (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).
- [E3] Data residency & backup sweep: deletion propagation and confirmation — Infrastructure & DR technical follow-up, 2026-08-03 — `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/rishi_malhotra/20260807-data-sovereignty-backup-sweep-qa.json` (`dsid_5af161cb46d6483abc0eea8167a63147`).

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention support rule — corrected\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/hosted-api-retention-support-rule-corrected-ntion_v2.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Ethan Park\n\n# Hosted API retention support rule — corrected\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-16T04:01:18.911646+00:00\nConfidence: 0.95\nOwner: Ethan Park\nTags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected\n\n## Summary\n\nCorrected Hosted rule: request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default, embeddings 14 days, ephemeral caches under one hour unless explicitly persisted, and model artifacts until deletion.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule\nSource: Platform & Console policy\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-v1\n\n# Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule\n\n**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  \n**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  \n**Revision:** 1 (baseline)  \n**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park\n\n## Rule\n\nUse the following statements for Hosted API inquiries:\n\n- By default, prompts, inputs, and model outputs are processed to fulfill the request and are not persisted as durable application data. Redwood does not use Customer Content processed through the service to train foundation models.\n- Redwood retains non-content operational metadata for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning. Platform logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.\n- In-memory caches are ephemeral and are not intended as durable Customer Content storage.\n- A customer may request deletion through its account team or Support. Redwood verifies authorization and scope, deletes applicable durable stores, and confirms completion.\n- Residual data can remain temporarily in backups/disaster-recovery systems until rotation and in logs required for security, reliability, legal, or compliance purposes.\n- Where available, customers may select a serving region. Redwood aims to keep inference processing in that region, but control-plane data, centralized non-content monitoring, and Support workflows can have different residency characteristics.\n- Retention and audit-log controls vary by plan and configuration.\n\n## Do not promise\n\nDo not state a universal retention period, deletion SLA, backup-purge deadline, certificate format, or that all data always remains in-region unless the customer's contract and deployment have been validated.\n\n## Explicit unknowns\n\nThe current approved overview does not establish:\n\n- a Hosted-wide time to delete active data;\n- a maximum time to remove data from backups or disaster-recovery media;\n- tenant-termination-specific sequencing;\n- whether deletion confirmation includes backup exhaustion;\n- a Hosted-wide cross-region replication rule;\n- a universal audit-log retention period.\n\n## Validation steps before answering a customer",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency — support rule\nSource: Platform & Console policy\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-correction\n\n# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency — support rule\n\n**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  \n**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  \n**Revision:** 2 (corrected; replaces revision 1)  \n**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park\n\n## Canonical Hosted defaults\n\nUse these defaults only when the customer's contract or configured policy does not replace them:\n\n- Request/response payloads: retained 30 days by default.\n- Embeddings and derived vectors: retained 14 days by default.\n- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly persists them.\n- Model artifacts, including fine-tuned artifacts: retained until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default cadence, while the maximum default backup-retention/full-scrub window is 90 days.\n- Deletion and erasure audit events: retained 365 days by default and available through the Console or export for eligible enterprise accounts.\n- Customer Content is not used to train Redwood foundation models.\n\nRetention can be changed by plan, configuration, or contract. Do not imply that the default payload retention is zero.\n\n## Verified erasure or tenant termination\n\n1. Verify requester authorization and exact scope.\n2. Stop serving the terminated tenant immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge.\n3. Purge primary data within 30 days after the verified erasure request or tenant termination.\n4. Scrub backups and replicated snapshots within 90 days. This window accounts for backup lifecycle and cross-region replication.\n5. Provide a deletion attestation on request after completion.\n\nLater infrastructure evidence describes targeted backup deletion through tombstone scrubs or snapshot rehydration/rewrite. Those paths can finish sooner, but their timing depends on dataset size, snapshot immutability, governance, and the customer's agreement. Do not convert typical 24–72-hour or 3–10-day mechanics into a universal SLA. Evidence should distinguish the primary-delete timestamp from the backup-sweep completion timestamp.\n\n## Residency and cross-region behavior",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency — support rule\nSource: Platform & Console policy\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-correction\n\ntiming depends on dataset size, snapshot immutability, governance, and the customer's agreement. Do not convert typical 24–72-hour or 3–10-day mechanics into a universal SLA. Evidence should distinguish the primary-delete timestamp from the backup-sweep completion timestamp.\n\n## Residency and cross-region behavior\n\n- Hosted data is persisted in the tenant's primary region.\n- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA and configuration.\n- For an EU-only/region-locked contractual commitment, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\n- Region selection alone does not prove that control-plane data, non-content global monitoring, or Support-submitted content has the same residency boundary.\n\n## Evidence available for deletion\n\nDeletion/erasure events are auditable. Depending on plan and contract, evidence can include a completion attestation, Console record, audit export, request ID, primary-purge timestamp, backup-sweep completion timestamp, operator ID, affected snapshot/object identifiers, and a verification hash. Do not promise a particular certificate format or delivery deadline unless it is contracted.\n\n## Remaining unknowns and exceptions\n\nThe available evidence does not establish:\n\n- that every customer has the same configured retention values;\n- a universal sub-30-day primary-purge SLA or sub-90-day backup-purge SLA;\n- that snapshot immutability can always be overridden;\n- a universal evidence format or attestation-delivery time;\n- that legal or compliance holds can never delay deletion;\n- that all control-plane, telemetry, or Support data is tenant-region bound.\n\n## Validation steps before customer use",

            "content": "# Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule\n\n**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  \n**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  \n**Revision:** 1 (baseline)  \n**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park\n\n## Rule\n\nUse the following statements for Hosted API inquiries:\n\n- By default, prompts, inputs, and model outputs are processed to fulfill the request and are not persisted as durable application data. Redwood does not use Customer Content processed through the service to train foundation models.\n- Redwood retains non-content operational metadata for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning. Platform logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.\n- In-memory caches are ephemeral and are not intended as durable Customer Content storage.\n- A customer may request deletion through its account team or Support. Redwood verifies authorization and scope, deletes applicable durable stores, and confirms completion.\n- Residual data can remain temporarily in backups/disaster-recovery systems until rotation and in logs required for security, reliability, legal, or compliance purposes.\n- Where available, customers may select a serving region. # Hosted API retention and deletion — support rule

**Audience:** Support and customer-facing responders  
**Scope:** Redwood API (Hosted) only  
**Revision:** 1 (baseline)  
**Owner:** Platform & Console — Ethan Park

## Rule

Use the following statements for Hosted API inquiries:

- By default, prompts, inputs, and model outputs are processed to fulfill the request and are not persisted as durable application data. Redwood does not use Customer Content processed through the service to train foundation models.
- Redwood retains non-content operational metadata for reliability, abuse prevention, billing, and capacity planning. Platform logs are designed to avoid Customer Content by default.
- In-memory caches are ephemeral and are not intended as durable Customer Content storage.
- A customer may request deletion through its account team or Support. Redwood verifies authorization and scope, deletes applicable durable stores, and confirms completion.
- Residual data can remain temporarily in backups/disaster-recovery systems until rotation and in logs required for security, reliability, legal, or compliance purposes.
- Where available, customers may select a serving region. Redwood aims to keep inference processing in that region, but control-plane data, centralized non-content monitoring, and Support workflows can have different residency characteristics.
- Retention and audit-log controls vary by plan and configuration.

## Do not promise

Do not state a universal retention period, deletion SLA, backup-purge deadline, certificate format, or that all data always remains in-region unless the customer's contract and deployment have been validated.

## Explicit unknowns

The current approved overview does not establish:

- a Hosted-wide time to delete active data;
- a maximum time to remove data from backups or disaster-recovery media;
- tenant-termination-specific sequencing;
- whether deletion confirmation includes backup exhaustion;
- a Hosted-wide cross-region replication rule;
- a universal audit-log retention period.

## Validation steps before answering a customer
